transcript:
User: Hi, we saw your service. Our intake calls after hours keep going to voicemail.
Agent: Got it, thanks for sharing that — those intake calls after hours going to voicemail add up. After you close for the day, what usually happens with those callers… do they tend to leave a message, or do they just call the next place?
User: Most leave a message, but we estimate about 70% would book if someone answered live.
Agent: Yeah, that makes total sense — when someone actually answers, they almost always book. Just so I understand your world a bit better, what kind of business are you running (vet clinic, medical office, home services, something else)?
User: We are a personal injury law firm based in New York, called Bell & Associates Legal.
Agent: Got it, thanks for sharing that — PI intake in New York is super competitive, so those after-hours calls really matter. Roughly how many after-hours intake calls would you say hit voicemail in a typical week?
User: About 12 missed calls a week go to voicemail.
Agent: That’s really helpful — 12 missed PI intake calls a week in New York is a lot of potential cases. When those callers hit voicemail instead of a live answer, how concerned are you that they’re just hanging up and calling the next firm?
User: We're quite concerned. If someone answered, we believe about 70% would book an appointment with us.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — in PI, losing even a few of those live conversations can mean walking away from real cases. So… ballpark, when you do sign a new client from an intake, what’s the average fee you collect on a typical case (just a rough number is fine)?
User: The average intake value for us is about $1,800 per case.
Agent: That’s really clear, thank you — with your numbers, those 12 missed calls a week and a 70% book rate, you’re quietly leaking about $65,000 a month in potential revenue. So, to actually fix this, would you be open to a quick 20‑minute walkthrough this week where we show you exactly how we’d stop those after‑hours intakes from going to voicemail — is later today or tomorrow better for you?
User: Sure, I'd be open to a walkthrough. Tomorrow would work better for me.
Agent: Got it, tomorrow’s better — calendar-wise the first openings are actually Wednesday and Thursday afternoon Eastern. I can get you in as soon as Wednesday at 2:45 or 6:30 Eastern for a 20‑minute call with Jay, no commitment — which of those works better for you?
User: Wednesday at 2:45 Eastern works for me. Yes, book it.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Perfect, you’re all set — we’ve got you booked for Wednesday at 2:45 Eastern with Jay. You’ll get an SMS confirmation with all the details, and you can add it to your calendar or reschedule from there if anything changes. Is there anything else I can help you with before we hop off?
